 The Social Security Administration confirmed that Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients will receive two payments in December.

 Translated and edited by   El Cronista EN Published on November 12, 2026 2:34 PM abre en nueva pestaña abre en nueva pestaña abre en nueva pestaña abre en nueva pestaña En esta noticia What are the two most important dates for these SSA beneficiaries in December 2026? 
 Why do SSI recipients get two payments in December? 
 How much of a COLA increase will SSI receive for 2027? 
 The Social Security Administration (SSA) set two Supplemental Security Income payment dates in December 2026 . The schedule includes an early payment for January, so beneficiaries will receive two deposits in the same month. 
 The agency also confirmed a boost based on the Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) for its 2027 benefits. This increase will take effect earlier than usual for SSI recipients , who will receive the new amount in their second December payment. 
 Deposits . By order of Section 202(y) of the Social Security Act, the SSA will stop paying monthly benefits to foreign nationals who do not meet this requirement abre en nueva pestaña Money . Extra cash! A $1,330 refund is available to low- and middle-income families who meet these requirements: No Social Security number needed abre en nueva pestaña What are the two most important dates for these SSA beneficiaries in December 2026?
 SSI recipients will receive their payments on these two dates: 
 December 1, 2026: deposit for the December benefit. 
 December 31, 2026: advance payment for January 2027, which will already include the COLA increase. 
 Why do SSI recipients get two payments in December?
 The SSA advances January’s payment because Jan. 1 is a federal holiday (New Year’s Day). When the usual payment date falls on a weekend or holiday, the agency sends the transfer on the previous business day. 
 So the second deposit is not an extra benefit, but the January 2027 payment. 
 How much of a COLA increase will SSI receive for 2027?
 The SSA confirmed a 3.6% increase for 2027 , which will also apply to SSI recipients. According to the agency, the new adjustment will take effect for these recipients with the Dec. 31, 2026, deposit. 
 The maximum monthly federal benefit will rise from: 
 $994 to $1,029 for one person. 
 $1,491 to $1,544 for an eligible couple. 
 Individual amounts may vary depending on income and other eligibility conditions.
